verdict.rationale: vLLM's own docs state support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and multiple CPU architectures, plus hardware plugins for TPUs, Gaudi, Ascend, MetaX GPUs and others. They also claim it can run any model on any hardware. However, the evidence never explicitly describes vendor-specific acceleration kernels. The NVFP4 quantization support and per-scheme backend overrides only hint at hardware-tuned paths. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of vendor-specific kernels per GPU vendor (e.g., CUDA vs ROCm kernel paths), per-vendor installation/feature-parity details, independent or hands-on corroboration of non-NVIDIA performance.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run models on NVIDIA, AMD, or other GPU vendors using vendor-specific acceleration kernels

citations.quote: Support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and x86/ARM/PowerPC CPUs. Additionally, diverse hardware plugins such as Google TPUs, Intel Gaudi, IBM Spyre, Huawei Ascend, Rebellions NPU, Apple Silicon, MetaX GPU, and more.
Run any model on any hardware.
use `linear_backend_per_quant` to override the backend for individual schemes
